subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: If a, b, c are in arithmetic progression, show that ax + by + c = 0 represents a family of concurrent lines, and find the point of concurrency.

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IB (2026-27 edition), chapter 3 THE STRAIGHT LINE, Very Short Answer question 16, book p.142. Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the volume prints a chapter-level marks banner over this section but no per-step allocation on any answer. The 1+1 split gives the first mark for turning the arithmetic progression into a − 2b + c = 0, and the second for matching that against ax + by + c = 0 and naming the point; the question asks for two things, so the split follows them. Paper position: Maths-1B Section A runs Q1 to Q10 at 2 marks each, all compulsory, under the 2026-27 pattern. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Answer checked by substitution: putting x = 1, y = −2 into ax + by + c gives a − 2b + c, which the arithmetic progression makes 0 for every such a, b, c. Tested on one member of the family, a = 1, b = 2, c = 3: the line x + 2y + 3 = 0 gives 1 − 4 + 3 = 0 at (1, −2). Tested on a second, a = 5, b = 3, c = 1: the line 5x + 3y + 1 = 0 gives 5 − 6 + 1 = 0 at the same point.

recall_prompt: Say how you would solve this — say what arithmetic progression gives you, and how you read the fixed point off it.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Write the arithmetic progression condition
steps.margin_note: First mark. Arithmetic progression means equal gaps, so b − a = c − b. Rearranged as a − 2b + c = 0, the condition already looks like a line equation with a, b, c as the variables.
steps.memory_tip: Arithmetic progression means equal gaps: b − a = c − b, so 2b = a + c.
lines: Given a, b, c are in A.P.

recall.must_convey: That a, b, c in arithmetic progression gives b − a = c − b, that is a − 2b + c = 0.
accept: b minus a equals c minus b
two b equals a plus c

reject: the point of concurrency is one comma minus two
heard_as: two b equals a plus c

steps.why: The given line has a, b, c as its coefficients, so a relation among a, b, c is the only usable information, and it must be written in the same shape as the line before it can be compared.
common_mistakes: Writing 2b = a − c instead of 2b = a + c.
Using b/a = c/b, which is the geometric progression condition.

steps.label: Read the fixed point
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Write (1) with the coefficients in the same order as the line. The numbers standing beside a and b are then the coordinates of the fixed point.
steps.memory_tip: Write the condition as a(x) + b(y) + c = 0. The numbers beside a and b are the fixed point.
lines: Given line is ax + by + c = 0   ……(2)
for every a, b, c in A.P.  (a, b not both 0)
∴ all the lines pass through one fixed point

recall.must_convey: That a − 2b + c = 0 is a(1) + b(−2) + c = 0, so every line of the family passes through (1, −2).
accept: write it as a into one plus b into minus two plus c
compare the condition with a x plus b y plus c
x is one and y is minus two
condition ni line tho compare cheyyali
the point of concurrency is one comma minus two
reject: b minus a equals c minus b

steps.why: Concurrent means all the lines pass through one common point. Since (1, −2) satisfies the line for every choice of a, b, c allowed by the condition, that single point is common to the whole family.
common_mistakes: Giving the point as (1, 2) and losing the minus sign that came from −2b.
Solving two particular lines instead of matching the condition, which takes far longer than two marks allow.
